reviewer: Codex / Deep single-agent engineering review; user-authorized 2.8.3 renewal

areas.SEC-01: Node CLI protects local installation destinations, user-owned skills, receipts, fetched update sources, security notes and npm publication; no network server or database runtime is shipped.
areas.SEC-02: Installation and security persistence reject linked paths and preserve user-owned files; update checks do not grant publication or global mutation. Focused ownership/rollback tests are required.
areas.SEC-03: Filesystem writes, artifact access and update effects are authorized at CLI command boundaries and constrained by ownership/path checks; security gate negative cases and install transaction tests exercise those boundaries.
areas.SEC-04: This CLI does not implement end-user accounts, organization memberships, sessions or account suspension. Credential rotation remains an operator responsibility under SEC-08/09.
areas.SEC-05: Publishing requires actual protected release workflow and npm trusted-publisher environment inspection; cannot be inferred from build output or local files.
areas.SEC-06: No end-user login, password storage, account recovery or session service exists in the shipped CLI. npm publication authentication remains separately required under SEC-09.
areas.SEC-07: CLI inputs are bounded, Git bindings require exact object IDs, note writes reject traversal and links, deployment hashes are remeasured; security and external update tests cover adversarial inputs. No web upload or HTML rendering service is present.
areas.SEC-08: Package secret scanning and note redaction/path tests run on the exact snapshot. Runtime proof stores sanitized check names, exit codes and output hashes, never raw subprocess output or credential values.
areas.SEC-09: Reviewed executable closure includes source, scripts, package manifest, dependency lock, compiler config and workflows. Exact target tests, action commit pins, npm high severity audit and package secret checks must pass. External branch/environment enforcement is separately verified.

limitations: Digest inventory detects divergence from identified engineering review; it is not a comprehensive code audit.
Sensitive source or executable changes require renewed review rather than automatic approval.
Remote deployment state and installed dependency provenance are not proved by source hashes alone.
review_notes: Reviewed hook schema migration: opt-in, backup and file identity checks, handler preservation, no Codex trust bypass; existing same-user filesystem race limitation retained.
Reviewed hook discovery: bounded separate app-server probe, exact command/source matching, trust and event coverage separated from current-session execution.
Reviewed local observations: opt-in private hash-only records, symlink/hardlink checks, drift validation, explicitly not host attestation.

Reviewed memory completeness: missing/empty/invalid/unreadable/incomplete states, no overwrite after incomplete read, sanitized diagnostics; memory remains user-owned and is not an adversarial same-user sandbox.
Reviewed updater: fixed official exact-version npm tarball URL, no redirects or credentials, bounded metadata and HEAD availability only; 404 fails closed before installation.

Reviewed skill-content scanner and focused tests: bounded traversal/bytes, regular-file identity checks, no raw secret output; heuristic checks do not prove comprehensive privacy or offline execution.
Reviewed manifest and lock: patch version only, no dependency graph changes; CI policy and workflow source are unchanged.

Reviewed 2.8.3 turn scope: canonical repository/session keys, bounded index and dirty-content fingerprints, generated filtering before reads, include precedence, private hash-only baseline, stale/corrupt/missing state downgraded to manual inspection; no authentication or security attestation claim.

Reviewed advisory/strict split: Deep/Mission alone do not promote read-only work, risky selected changes receive one correction pass, explicit CLI and commit/push/deploy security contracts remain unchanged.
Reviewed report-title parsing and narrower database file classification, focused fixtures and package scripts; no dependency graph change, no automatic publication or global install.

Remaining limits: without host turn IDs overlapping work cannot be attributed independently; same-OS-user filesystem races and arbitrary Windows reparse points remain outside the baseline threat guarantee.
